findings.description: SHEET-MAP-001 says only 'resolve a ledger Symbol to its GOOGLEFINANCE ticker via config's alias map (identity when unset)' — nothing about case or whitespace. The real `resolve_ticker` does `symbol.trim().to_uppercase()` BEFORE consulting `AliasMap::resolve`, and the identity fallback returns that NORMALIZED form, not the raw input (pinned by mapping.rs's `resolve_ticker_normalizes_case_and_whitespace_before_alias_lookup`: `"brk"`/`" BRK "`/`" brk"` → `"BRK.B"`; `" amzn "` → `"AMZN"`, not `"amzn"` or `" amzn "`). All 3 A sketches, built from the EARS text alone, uniformly omit normalization entirely — raw map lookup, raw-text identity fallback, no trim/uppercase anywhere. All 3 B reconstructions, built from the code alone, independently and near-verbatim surface this exact trim→uppercase→lookup pipeline (and its normalized-identity-fallback corollary) as core, test-pinned behavior that the given EARS text never states. Same gap visible from both sides: the EARS under-specifies normalization; the code (and its tests) hard-enforce it.

All 3 A sketches invent defensive quote-escaping of the ticker before embedding it in the formula (`ticker.replace('"', "\"\"")` / equivalent), reasoning that alias values are 'free-form config input.' The real `price_formula`/`quote_date_formula` do no escaping at all: `format!("=GOOGLEFINANCE(\"{ticker}\",\"price\")")` interpolates the ticker raw, with no sanitization and no test covering embedded-quote tickers. Spec silence on malformed-ticker handling produced a uniform A-side robustness feature that doesn't exist in — and isn't required by — the real implementation.

All 3 A sketches model `Symbol` as a dedicated newtype struct (`Symbol(pub String)`, deriving `Eq`/`Hash`/`Clone`) used as an alias-map key. The real `Symbol` (in both `ledger_core` and `config`) is a plain `pub type Symbol = String` alias, not a distinct struct — `AliasMap` is keyed directly on `String`/`Symbol`. Low behavioral impact (String already has Eq/Hash) but a stable, unanimous structural invention the EARS text neither confirms nor rules out.

All 3 B reconstructions fold the Quote Date companion-cell contract into the same requirement set: it must use the IDENTICAL resolved ticker as that row's Price formula, in the exact form `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("<ticker>","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")` — matching `quote_date_formula` verbatim and pinned character-for-character by formula.rs's `positions_carries_a_locale_proof_quote_date_companion_column` (including the aliased-ticker check `NASDAQ:AMZN`). The given SHEET-MAP-001 text says nothing about a Quote Date cell — it speaks only to building 'the Price formula from the resolved ticker.' This is a fully enforced, heavily-tested behavior that the audited EARS text is silent on (it may belong to a sibling/undisclosed EARS ID, but relative to the text given, it is unstated).

All 3 B outputs pin the Price formula's literal syntax down to the character (no space after the ticker's closing quote-comma: `...","price")`), and pin an explicit 'must NOT contain the raw unresolved symbol' test assertion (formula.rs / mapping.rs: `assert!(!price.contains("\"BRK\""))`). SHEET-MAP-001 only says 'build the Price formula from the resolved ticker' — silent on exact syntax. Weak/secondary finding: A independently guessed the `"price"` attribute correctly, so this mostly restates something the A direction already got right rather than exposing a fresh gap.
